review_type: same-case nonblind AI independent selected-source entailment review

inputs_actually_read.read_scope: full wire JSON; full system instructions; reconstructed 71 exact source fragments, original 10 full claims, 19 syntactic units and each actual binding/allowed scope; lookup candidates not proof
provider_result.raw_text parsed without rewriting; observed validation metadata for structural qualification only

method.proof_scope: Only a unit’s actually selected complete fragments count as proof. Original full claim resolves semantic inheritance, but is not source evidence. No claim-union/sibling evidence borrowing.
method.fragment_join_rule: Distinct immutable fragments remain distinct. Meaning-preserving paraphrases and necessary, unambiguous selected-text inferences are allowed; adjacency, shared words and candidate matches alone are not entailment.
method.predicate_assignment: Explicit predicates and appositions are assigned to the unit containing them; object-only segments inherit a necessary shared predicate. ATP U03 shared reduce ownership is qualified below. The carbohydrate/glucose boundary is separately qualified.
method.reason_rule: A literal part-to-FID mapping names an asserted scientific part and its corresponding selected ID; merely listing FIDs is not such a mapping.
method.claim_rule: A claim is complete iff all its independently assessed units are complete.

qualifications.issue: The object-only text which ATP inherits the shared reduce-to-G3P predicate under semantic reading; only F058 is selected. If classification is assigned only to the textual U04, U03 becomes complete.

The relative clause is assessed for the carbohydrate six-carbon/six-turn relationship explicitly proved by F002/F005. Commonly glucose is a U01 apposition. If an audit duplicates the full antecedent’s glucose identity into U02, F002/F005 alone do not name glucose and U02 becomes partial; sibling F001 must then be explicitly selected rather than borrowed.

The opening chloroplast-has-three-carbon-atoms continuation is clipped and must not certify that entity property. Its independent main clause explicitly states three turns of the Calvin cycle fix enough net carbon to export one G3P, which is the asserted relation in the reviewed units. No missing F010 is silently reconstructed for these judgments.

selected_complete_fragment_texts.exact_text: One of the G3P molecules leaves the Calvin cycle to contribute to the formation of the carbohydrate molecule, which is commonly glucose (C6H12O6).
Because the carbohydrate molecule has six carbon atoms, it takes six turns of the Calvin cycle to make one carbohydrate molecule (one for each carbon dioxide molecule fixed).
The remaining G3P molecules regenerate RuBP, which enables the system to prepare for the carbon-fixation step.
ATP is also used in the regeneration of RuBP.

FIGURE 5.15 The Calvin cycle has three stages. In stage 1, the enzyme RuBisCO incorporates carbon dioxide into an organic molecule. In stage 2, the organic molecule is reduced. In stage 3, RuBP, the molecule that starts the cycle, is regenerated so that the cycle can continue. In summary, it takes six turns of the Calvin cycle to fix six carbon atoms from CO2. These six turns require energy input from 12 ATP molecules and 12 NADPH molecules in the reduction step and 6 ATP molecules in the regeneration step.

Stage 3: Regeneration Interestingly, at this point, only one of the G3P molecules leaves the Calvin cycle and is sent to the cytoplasm to contribute to the formation of other compounds needed by the plant.
chloroplast has three carbon atoms, it takes three “turns” of the Calvin cycle to fix enough net carbon to export one G3P.
But each turn makes two G3Ps, thus three turns make six G3Ps.
One is exported while the remaining five G3P molecules remain in the cycle and are used to regenerate RuBP, which enables the system to prepare for more CO2 to be fixed.
The resulting six-carbon compound is broken down into two three-carbon compounds, and the energy in ATP and NADPH is used to convert these molecules into G3P.
The remaining G3P molecules stay in the cycle to be formed back into RuBP, which is ready to react with more CO2.
In the stroma, in addition to CO2, two other chemicals are present to initiate the Calvin cycle: an enzyme abbreviated RuBisCO, and the molecule ribulose bisphosphate (RuBP).
RuBisCO catalyzes a reaction between CO2 and RuBP, which forms a six-carbon compound that is immediately converted into two three-carbon compounds.
This process is called carbon fixation, because CO2 is “fixed” from its inorganic form into organic molecules.
ATP and NADPH use their stored energy to convert the three-carbon compound, 3-PGA, into another three-carbon compound called G3P.
This type of reaction is called a reduction reaction, because it involves the gain of electrons.

Stage 1: Fixation In the stroma, in addition to CO2, two other components are present to initiate the light-independent reactions: an enzyme called ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate carboxylase/oxygenase (RuBisCO), and three molecules of ribulose bisphosphate (RuBP), as shown in Figure 8.19.
